fixes.explanation: Yes, baker! Joab, David's army commander, sends messengers to say, “I have fought against Rabbah and have captured the water supply of the city.” Think about that for a second. He has the city's water, and the city is still standing there. I bet that message came with a big grin.
That's it, baker. Joab says, “Otherwise I will capture the city, and it will be named after me.” Joab is David's army commander. He's telling the king to come take it, or Joab's name goes on it.

All of them, baker! The text says David assembled all the troops and went to Rabbah. Joab had asked for the rest of the troops, and David brought everybody. Then he fought against the city and captured it (2 Samuel 12:28–29).

Half sounds reasonable, friend, but that's not what the text says. David assembled all the troops and went to Rabbah. He brought the whole army. Half the troops would have been a different story, and a smaller one.
Right on, baker. David took the crown from the head of the Ammonites' king. Then that crown was placed on David's head. It's the crown that ended up on a new head.

A turban is a good guess for something sitting on a head, friend. But the text says David took the crown from the head of the Ammonites' king. No turban anywhere in these verses. I'd have guessed turban too, and I would have been just as wrong, so we're in this together.
True, baker. The text says David took a great amount of plunder from the city. That's on top of the crown, so the crown wasn't the whole haul. Rabbah gave up a lot.
This one's true, friend. After the crown, the text says David took a great amount of plunder from the city. It wasn't just a crown. He took a lot more.
To Jerusalem, baker. The text says, “Then David and all his troops returned to Jerusalem.” Everybody went back together. That's where this passage ends.
Hebron is a fair guess, friend, but it's not in this passage. The text says David and all his troops returned to Jerusalem. That's where the whole army went.

Bethlehem is a fine guess, baker, but the text points somewhere else. It says David and all his troops returned to Jerusalem. Bethlehem never comes up in these verses. Jerusalem is the stop on this map.
